claim: Lovable mobile app syncs projects between phone and desktop so a user can pick up exactly where they left off.
quote: Switch seamlessly between phone and computer. Whatever you start in one place continues exactly where you left it in the other.

claim: Lovable launched a free iOS and Android mobile app on April 27, 2026 that lets non-technical users iterate on web apps from their phone using voice or text prompts.
quote: Lovable released its mobile app on April 27, 2026, bringing its AI-powered vibe coding capabilities to iOS and Android platforms.

claim: Lovable supports sign-in via Google, GitHub, or email and uses that identity to manage the dashboard where all of a user's projects are stored.
quote: Lovable supports authentication through Google, GitHub, or email. After signing in, the Lovable platform creates a default dashboard where all projects are managed.

claim: Lovable's Versioning 2.0 groups edits by date like Google Docs, adds bookmarks for milestone versions, and lets users restore older versions which appear as new edit cards (similar to git revert).
quote: Restore to earlier versions of your app more easily by using bookmarks and our improved history view.

claim: Lovable's free plan gives 5 daily credits up to a maximum of 30 per calendar month, with each message consuming credits based on complexity — a tight ceiling for follow-up iteration.
quote: 5 daily credits, up to a maximum of 30 per month. Daily credits are being reset every day at midnight UTC. On a free plan you can use a total of 30 free credits per calendar month.

claim: Bolt.new's free tier provides 1M tokens per month with a 300K daily cap and no credit card required, enough for several small apps but tokens do not roll over.
quote: Bolt.new's free plan provides 1M tokens per month with a 300K daily limit. This is enough for 2-5 small full-stack apps or one mid-size MVP.

claim: Bolt.new keeps a version history timeline and restoring an earlier version does not change the current Bolt or Supabase databases.
quote: Version history (which you can see using the View history button) is a timeline of changes, letting you see how your project has evolved. Restoring to an earlier project version will not change your current Bolt or Supabase databases.

claim: v0 retains conversation context and chat history across sessions so iteration builds on prior state rather than re-exploring the code each time.
quote: The agentic system remembers context from your conversation, so each iteration builds on the previous one.

claim: v0's free plan gives $5 in monthly credits with a 7-message-per-day cap, the most restrictive of the major tools for follow-up edits.
quote: The free tier includes $5 in monthly credits, which resets each billing cycle... The Free plan includes a 7-message/day limit.

claim: Replit Mobile Apps lets users go from idea to a published native iOS app via Replit Agent on a phone, with QR-code preview on a physical device through Expo.
quote: Mobile Apps on Replit, a new way to go from idea to fully published app using natural language.

claim: Replit's iPhone vibe-coding app went four months without updates due to an App Store review dispute, illustrating fragility of the mobile iteration path for non-technical alumni.
quote: Replit CEO Amjad Masad shared that the company and Apple resolved an issue that resulted in four months without any app updates.

claim: Replit supports continuous deployment where every change pushed to GitHub from the Version Control tab triggers an automatic redeployment, so iteration ships without a manual redeploy button.
quote: Every change you push to GitHub from the Version Control tab triggers an automatic redeployment.

claim: Most vibe-coding tools generate code and hand it over rather than maintain the running app, leaving alumni responsible for re-opening and iterating themselves to keep an app live months later.
quote: The CRM dashboard you vibe-coded in March is still accurate and maintained in September.
